title: Mati Aharoni
name: Mati Aharoni
summary: Mati Aharoni is a penetration-testing practitioner and the founder of Offensive Security, best known for helping create Kali Linux, a Debian-based distribution used for security assessment and training.
whyThisMatters: Aharoni helped turn a specialist collection of assessment tools into a maintained, widely documented platform. Kali Linux and the training ecosystem around Offensive Security made repeatable lab work and security testing more accessible to practitioners.
knownFor: Co-creating Kali Linux as the successor to BackTrack
Supporting a distribution designed for penetration testing and security auditing
Building training and community resources around hands-on security assessment

sections.overview:
Mati Aharoni is known in the security community by the handle muts. He founded Offensive Security and worked on the transition from BackTrack to Kali Linux, a distribution intended for penetration testing and security auditing.

Kali Linux was developed by Offensive Security as a Debian-based successor to BackTrack. Its documentation emphasizes that its purpose is professional security assessment, rather than a general-purpose operating system; that framing matters because the included tools must be used lawfully and with authorization.

Aharoni's contribution is therefore as much infrastructural as individual: maintaining a common environment for training, research, and testing helps practitioners reproduce work, exchange methods, and learn responsible assessment practice.

timeline.event: Offensive Security begins operating in the penetration-testing and training community.
Aharoni contacts Debian consultant Raphaël Hertzog about building BackTrack's successor on Debian.
Kali Linux is released as the Debian-based successor to BackTrack.
Kali Linux remains maintained as a security-assessment distribution with official documentation and verification guidance.
